slides.headline: Huawei was found guilty in the US. Why it matters
slides.subline: **Explained:** what the jury decided, and what happens next.
slides.credit: Raysonho @ Open Grid Scheduler / Grid Engine / CC0 (file photo)

slides.body: On Tuesday a US jury convicted Huawei on **10 of 12 charges**, including [[conspiracy to steal trade secrets]], bank fraud and sanctions violations.
Jurors **acquitted** Huawei of the most serious charge: a [[racketeering conspiracy]], a charge usually used against organised crime.
Prosecutors said Huawei stole secrets from US firms and did business in **Iran and North Korea**. The case began in [[2018]]. In 2019 the US put Huawei on a trade blacklist.
Its lawyers said investigators used **isolated incidents** by a few of 200,000+ employees to build a false story. Huawei says it plans to [[appeal]].
Experts say the case has **not hurt** Huawei’s business. It diversified and is now a key player in China’s [[AI push]]. Does a US verdict change how you see Huawei?
